title: Cocktail 2 Is the Most Anticipated Indian Film of the Year. The Internet Can't Pick a Side.
excerpt: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna have the internet splitting into teams like it's 2012 all over again. The trailer cracked the US Top 10. June 19 cannot come fast enough.
body:
Fourteen years after **Saif Ali Khan**, **Deepika Padukone**, and **Diana Penty** turned a Homi Adajania love triangle into a generational hit, the cocktail is being remixed — and the internet has already lost its mind.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg</youtube>

**Cocktail 2** just claimed the No. 1 spot on **IMDB's real-time most-anticipated Indian movies list** with a commanding 21% page view share. Its trailer has topped global YouTube charts, cracked the US Top 10, and social media is locked in the kind of passionate, irrational, deeply entertaining debate that only a good love triangle can produce: **Team Shahid-Kriti** or **Team Shahid-Rashmika**?

The answer, based on the trailer that dropped on June 2, is that you're supposed to agonise. That's the whole point.

## The Setup

**Shahid Kapoor** plays Kunal. **Rashmika Mandanna** is Diya. **Kriti Sanon** is Ally. From what the trailer reveals — and it reveals just enough to hook without spoiling — their friendship curdles into romance, their romance curdles into chaos, and the summer they share becomes the kind of mess that takes years to clean up. Or doesn't get cleaned up at all.

Director **Homi Adajania** has described it as a film about "what happens when friendship crosses lines it was never supposed to cross." The writing, by **Luv Ranjan** and **Tarun Jain**, leans into the messy emotional territory that made the original *Cocktail* feel uncomfortably real beneath its glossy surface.

> "From friends to lovers to CHAOS, the perfect cocktail is back." — Official tagline

## The Chemistry Debate

Let's talk about the thing everyone is talking about.

Shahid and Kriti already proved they can generate heat — their pairing in *Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya* (2024) was one of that film's genuine bright spots. They have a playful, sparring energy that the trailer deploys with precision.

But it's Shahid and Rashmika that have caught people off guard. She's softer, more vulnerable in the trailer's emotional beats, and the contrast works. Where Kriti's Ally is all confidence and control, Rashmika's Diya radiates the kind of guileless warmth that makes the triangle feel genuinely complicated rather than conveniently arranged.

Fan edits are flooding Instagram. Reaction videos are dissecting every shared glance. The discourse is already so intense that entertainment sites are running polls. This is the pre-release energy every producer dreams about, and **Maddock Films** must be sleeping very well.

## The Numbers Game

Mounted on an estimated budget of **₹80 crore**, Cocktail 2 is neither the biggest bet Bollywood is making this June nor the smallest — but it might be the smartest. Romance drives repeat viewings. Love triangles drive conversation. And conversation, in 2026, drives theatrical openings.

The production pedigree is deliberately stacked. **Dinesh Vijan**'s Maddock Films has an almost absurd hit ratio in recent years (*Stree 2*, *Munjya*, the Maddock Horror Universe). **Luv Ranjan** co-writes and co-produces through Luv Films. Music is by **Pritam**, with lyrics by **Amitabh Bhattacharya** — the same combination that gave the original its iconic *Tum Hi Ho Bandhu*, which returns here in a new version that the trailer deploys like a precision emotional weapon.

Three songs have already dropped. *Jab Talak*, sung by **Arijit Singh** and **Akasa**, is pure romantic Bollywood comfort food — the kind of track that soundtracks reels for months.

## What Diaspora Audiences Should Know

**Cocktail 2** arrives in theatres globally on **June 19, 2026**. It's a wide release — expect it in every major US, UK, and Canadian multiplex that carries Indian films. Costumes are by **Anaita Shroff Adajania** (who styled the original), cinematography by **Santhana Krishnan Ravichandran**, and the film was partly shot in **Sicily** — so expect it to look gorgeous.

This is the kind of Bollywood film the diaspora turns out for: familiar emotional territory, star power that translates across geography, and a soundtrack designed to live in your head for months. The original *Cocktail* found an outsized audience in overseas markets, with many NRIs reminiscing about their own experiences of love and friendship, making the sequel's release a highly anticipated event. The film's themes resonate deeply with the Indian diaspora, who often navigate complex relationships across cultures. The sequel is betting on the same magic.

## The Verdict (So Far)

The trailer has done what trailers for love stories rarely manage: it made people care about who ends up with whom before they've seen a single scene. That's not marketing. That's casting. Shahid, Kriti, and Rashmika are each bringing something specific enough to the table that the triangle doesn't feel like a gimmick — it feels like a choice the audience has to make alongside the characters.

June 19. Pick your side. Pour the drink.
